UnitStatement: The dependency-extract skill is dispatched via TASK with TaskSkill: dependency-extract.
SCOPE is a required selector for deliverables, packages, or all deliverables under a run root.
The skill walks each in-scope deliverable folder and produces one register per deliverable.
RUN_ROOT is an optional path to the run workspace.
DECOMPOSITION_PATH is an optional explicit path to the latest decomposition markdown.
When DECOMPOSITION_PATH is omitted, the skill auto-discovers decomposition markdown under {RUN_ROOT}/_Decomposition/.
When no decomposition can be located, the run records [WARNING] MISSING_DECOMPOSITION in Run Notes.
Missing decomposition degrades validation and label resolution but does not fail the run.
SOURCE_DOCS defaults to AUTO and may be an explicit list of filenames or paths to scan per deliverable.
DOC_ROLE_MAP defaults to DEFAULT and may explicitly map ANCHOR_DOC and EXECUTION_DOCS filename patterns.
ANCHOR_DOC defaults to AUTO or an explicit filename or path and controls Pass 1 vertical Tree anchoring.
EXECUTION_DOC_ORDER defaults to AUTO or an ordered filename/path list and controls Pass 2 horizontal DAG execution-edge extraction.
MODE defaults to UPDATE and may be RESET_EXTRACTED.
STRICTNESS defaults to CONSERVATIVE and may be AGGRESSIVE.
AGGRESSIVE strictness permits strongly implied anchors only when marked ASSUMPTION with Confidence=LOW.
CONSUMER_CONTEXT defaults to NONE and may be TASK_ESTIMATING, AGGREGATION, or RECONCILIATION.
A non-NONE CONSUMER_CONTEXT adds a Downstream Handoff Notes section.
TASK_ESTIMATING consumer context attempts to populate ConsumerHint and EstimateImpactClass extension columns.
_REFERENCES.md is used to resolve document pointers for TargetType=DOCUMENT rows.
An existing Dependencies.csv register is used for match/merge and preserving declared edges.
An existing _DEPENDENCIES.md index is used to preserve declared lists and append Run History.
The skill outputs one dependency artifact set per in-scope deliverable.
Dependencies.csv uses the v3.1 schema with 29 required columns.
_DEPENDENCIES.md contains declared lists, extracted summary, run notes, run history, and lifecycle summary.
All runtime defaults and chosen paths must be recorded in _DEPENDENCIES.md Run Notes.
QA_CHECKS enumerates mandatory invariants and local quality checks for valid dependency-extract runs.
Each dependency row must cite at least one concrete evidence location or explicitly state location TBD.
The skill must never edit deliverable docs, _REFERENCES.md, or decomposition outputs.
Writes are limited to dependency artifacts: _DEPENDENCIES.md and Dependencies.csv.
If a target cannot be resolved confidently, TargetType must be UNKNOWN and the raw reference text preserved.
The skill does not create or restructure the decomposition Tree.
The skill only anchors to identifiers that already exist.
The skill requires no human decisions mid-run.
Conservative defaults must be logged.
Extracted rows no longer seen must be retired rather than deleted.
Notes must distinguish FACT, ASSUMPTION, and PROPOSAL epistemic states.
Dependencies.csv must remain parseable and include all 29 canonical required columns.
Legacy enum variants must be normalized to canonical enums on write.
The register tracks extraction lifecycle and closure lifecycle dimensions.
FromDeliverableID must match the current deliverable.
Unresolved targets must remain UNKNOWN or TBD rather than guessed.
Dependency edges represent information flow only, not coordination-only relationships or structural adjacency.
validate_dependencies_schema.py is the mandatory schema validation command for Dependencies.csv.
Schema validation confirms all 29 required v3.1 columns are present and the CSV is parseable.
DependencyID must be present and unique within the dependency register.
validate_enum.py validates enum fields on write.
Enum validation covers dependency class, anchor type, direction, dependency type, target type, explicitness, confidence, origin, status, and satisfaction status.
Legacy Direction values INBOUND and OUTBOUND normalize to UPSTREAM and DOWNSTREAM on write.
validate_id_format.sh validates ID fields such as deliverable and package identifiers.
ACTIVE rows must contain EvidenceFile and SourceRef or explicitly state location TBD.
_DEPENDENCIES.md counts must not contradict Dependencies.csv.
Obvious duplicate extracted rows must be merged or explicitly justified in Notes.
The parent anchor check counts ACTIVE ANCHOR rows with AnchorType=IMPLEMENTS_NODE.
Zero ACTIVE parent anchors require a [WARNING] FLOATING_NODE Run Notes entry.
Multiple ACTIVE parent anchors require a [WARNING] AMBIGUOUS_ANCHOR Run Notes entry.
A valid dependency-extract run leaves source documents in scope unmodified.
A valid run has an existing and parseable Dependencies.csv register.
A valid run includes required columns such as DependencyClass, AnchorType, and TargetRefID.
A valid run gives every ACTIVE row EvidenceFile and SourceRef or location TBD.
A valid run does not invent targets and permits UNKNOWN targets.
A valid run is non-destructive and does not delete rows.
A valid run has unique DependencyID values within each deliverable register.
A valid run writes canonical enum values.
A valid run keeps _DEPENDENCIES.md summary and lifecycle counts consistent with Dependencies.csv.
If decomposition is missing, Run Notes include [WARNING] MISSING_DECOMPOSITION and mark anchor validation and label resolution degraded.
[WARNING] FLOATING_NODE means no ACTIVE parent anchor exists.
[WARNING] AMBIGUOUS_ANCHOR means multiple ACTIVE parent anchors exist.
[WARNING] MISSING_DECOMPOSITION means decomposition could not be located and validation or label resolution is degraded.
When checks fail and cannot be conservatively repaired, files remain non-destructively updated.
Unrepaired check issues must be added explicitly to _DEPENDENCIES.md Run Notes.
Uncertain fields must be set to TBD or UNKNOWN rather than invented.
Dependencies.csv v3.1 has a fixed set of 29 required columns.
EstimateImpactClass and ConsumerHint are optional extension columns.
EstimateImpactClass and ConsumerHint are required only when CONSUMER_CONTEXT=TASK_ESTIMATING and evidence supports them.
dependency-extract extracts a Dependencies.csv v3.1 register from deliverable source documents using Anchor x Execution edge typing.
dependency-extract uses evidence-first provenance.
dependency-extract is a setup-pipeline skill dispatched by ORCHESTRATOR during project setup.
dependency-extract is compatible with Chirality TASK and control-loop refresh runs.
The TASK-enforced allowed tools are validate_dependencies_schema.py and validate_enum.py.
The skill extracts typed knowledge-graph edges from deliverable source documents.
The skill produces a deliverable-local dependency register made of Dependencies.csv v3.1 and _DEPENDENCIES.md.
Aggregation, reconciliation, estimating, and scheduling workflows can merge the dependency register into larger graphs.
Two-pass extraction preserves Tree x DAG knowledge-graph integrity.
Tree edges are emitted as DependencyClass=ANCHOR rows.
ANCHOR rows connect a deliverable to an existing definition node and optionally to requirement IDs.
DAG edges are emitted as DependencyClass=EXECUTION rows.
EXECUTION rows connect deliverables or other entities needed for prerequisites, handovers, constraints, or interfaces.
The skill does not build project-level graphs.
The skill produces only deliverable-local registers for downstream aggregation.
The suitable agent shell is TASK in generic shell mode with no profile.
ORCHESTRATOR dispatches dependency-extract during project setup or explicit refresh runs.
dependency-extract runs straight-through and never blocks on human decisions.
SCOPE is required and selects deliverables, packages, or ALL under the current run root.
RUN_ROOT is a path to the run workspace when available to the invoker.
DECOMPOSITION_PATH is the preferred explicit path to decomposition markdown.
When DECOMPOSITION_PATH is absent and RUN_ROOT exists, the most recent decomposition file under RUN_ROOT/_Decomposition is located.
When decomposition is missing, the skill records a warning and skips validation rather than guessing.
AUTO SOURCE_DOCS scans the deliverable folder for candidate source documents.
AUTO SOURCE_DOCS excludes dependency artifacts and obvious generated files.
DOC_ROLE_MAP roles are ANCHOR_DOC for definition or traceability signals and EXECUTION_DOCS for workflow or execution signals.
Default ANCHOR_DOC filename signals include datasheet, definition, requirements, scope, trace, and spec.
Default EXECUTION_DOCS filename signals include procedure, method, plan, workflow, guidance, and runbook.
AUTO ANCHOR_DOC chooses the highest-confidence match from DOC_ROLE_MAP and SOURCE_DOCS, otherwise the first source document.
AUTO EXECUTION_DOC_ORDER orders execution documents by likely workflow clarity and then remaining documents.
Defaults and chosen paths must be recorded in _DEPENDENCIES.md Run Notes.
_REFERENCES.md resolves document pointers or paths and conservatively populates TargetLocation for TargetType=DOCUMENT rows.
validate_dependencies_schema.py confirms Dependencies.csv has all 29 required v3.1 columns and is parseable.
validate_enum.py normalizes and validates dependency enum field values.
validate_id_format.sh validates deliverable, package, and WBS ID formats.
The skill must not edit source documents or _REFERENCES.md.
The skill must not edit decomposition outputs.
The skill must not write outside _DEPENDENCIES.md and Dependencies.csv.
The skill must not create or restructure the decomposition Tree.
The skill must not perform cross-deliverable synthesis.
Reads are limited to the current deliverable folder plus the decomposition document when available.
_REFERENCES.md is read in full when present to resolve TargetType=DOCUMENT rows.
Source documents in scope are read in full for anchor and execution-edge evidence extraction.
Existing Dependencies.csv is read in full for match/merge.
Existing _DEPENDENCIES.md is read in full to preserve declared lists and Run History.
DECOMPOSITION_PATH is read-only and is used to validate anchors and resolve canonical labels.
Writes are limited to dependency artifacts only.
_DEPENDENCIES.md is an allowed dependency artifact output.
Dependencies.csv is an allowed dependency artifact output.
No files outside the dependency artifacts may be created or modified.
Dependency extraction must run in two passes to preserve Tree x DAG integrity.
Pass 1 uses ANCHOR_DOC as the primary source.
Pass 1 emits exactly one parent anchor when possible.
Pass 1 emits zero or more trace anchors.
Parent-anchor signals include WBS Ref, Parent ID, Objective ID, and Scope Item ID.
Trace-anchor signals include traceability, requirements, requirement IDs, and compliance statements.
Anchor signals include tables or fields that map a deliverable to upstream definition identifiers.
ANCHOR rows set DependencyClass=ANCHOR.
ANCHOR rows set Direction=UPSTREAM.
Parent definition nodes use AnchorType=IMPLEMENTS_NODE.
Requirement trace links use AnchorType=TRACES_TO_REQUIREMENT.
ANCHOR rows use DependencyType=OTHER rather than execution dependency types.
Parent anchors use TargetType=WBS_NODE or the project's canonical definition-node type.
Requirement trace anchors use TargetType=REQUIREMENT.
Uncertain anchor target kinds use TargetType=UNKNOWN.
The decomposition document confirms whether a candidate anchor identifier exists.
The decomposition document resolves canonical labels for TargetName.
The decomposition document resolves stable deliverable and package IDs when referenced.
If decomposition is missing, the skill records [WARNING] MISSING_DECOMPOSITION and skips validation or label resolution.
CONSERVATIVE strictness emits ANCHOR rows only when identifiers appear explicitly.
AGGRESSIVE strictness may emit a plausible anchor only as ASSUMPTION with Confidence=LOW.
Pass 2 uses EXECUTION_DOC_ORDER as the primary source list.
Pass 2 emits EXECUTION rows for prerequisites, handoffs, constraints, and explicit information transfer.
Execution-edge signals include prerequisites, required inputs, approvals, and before-you-can language.
Execution-edge signals include outputs consumed by other deliverables.
Execution-edge signals include explicit data or artifact handoffs.
Execution-edge signals include constraints framed as requirements, approvals, or artifacts.
EXECUTION rows set DependencyClass=EXECUTION.
EXECUTION rows set AnchorType=NOT_APPLICABLE.
EXECUTION rows use canonical DependencyType values PREREQUISITE, INTERFACE, HANDOVER, CONSTRAINT, ENABLES, or OTHER.
Direction on EXECUTION rows is relative to this deliverable: UPSTREAM for inputs and DOWNSTREAM for outputs.
_REFERENCES.md is preferred for resolving mentioned document identifiers and names to stable pointers.
When resolving documents, TargetLocation prefers a local path when present.
When no local document path exists, TargetLocation records the best available pointer.
A dependency row must not be emitted solely because a reference is listed in _REFERENCES.md.
A listed reference becomes a dependency only when the source explicitly states it is required.
Dependency evidence must include EvidenceFile and SourceRef.
EvidenceQuote is optional and limited to 30 words or fewer.
Target resolution prefers exact matches to deliverable IDs defined by the decomposition.
The skill must not assume numeric deliverable ID formats.
When decomposition exists, target IDs are resolved by lookup.
When decomposition is missing, explicit IDs may be accepted as strings and other targets remain UNKNOWN.
Non-deliverable identifiers such as WBS, SSOW, OBJ, and REQ are accepted only when explicit.
Missing IDs must not be invented.
Uncertain targets keep TargetType=UNKNOWN.
Uncertain targets preserve the raw reference in TargetName or Statement.
Hypotheses are marked as PROPOSAL in Notes and are not upgraded to FACT.
Direction values INBOUND and OUTBOUND normalize to UPSTREAM and DOWNSTREAM.
Dependencies.csv is created when missing.
RegisterSchemaVersion must exist and be set to v3.1 for all rows.
Existing DependencyID values are preserved for matchable rows.
Found rows update LastSeen and set Status=ACTIVE.
Unseen extracted rows are marked RETIRED and not deleted.
Declared dependency edges with Origin=DECLARED are preserved.
FromDeliverableID must match the host deliverable identity.
DependencyID values must be unique within the deliverable register.
For non-deliverable targets, TargetDeliverableID must be empty and TargetRefID plus TargetName carry the stable reference.
For TargetType=DELIVERABLE, TargetDeliverableID must contain the stable deliverable ID.
Extracted row match/merge first uses exact DependencyID matches.
Extracted row match/merge next uses matching classification, target identifiers, and near-equivalent Statement.
Unmatched extracted rows receive new DependencyID values.
Function 4 keeps declared upstream and downstream dependency lists.
Function 4 adds or refreshes Extracted Dependency Register counts and compact table.
Function 4 adds or refreshes Run Notes with defaults, assumptions, paths, and warnings.
Function 4 appends one Run History entry per run.
Function 4 adds or refreshes Lifecycle Summary with ACTIVE, RETIRED, and closure-state counts.
Function 4 adds Downstream Handoff Notes only when CONSUMER_CONTEXT is not NONE.
Function 4 must not rename declared dependency sections.
Before finalizing files, Function 5 runs available deterministic local quality checks.
The parent anchor check counts ACTIVE rows with DependencyClass=ANCHOR and AnchorType=IMPLEMENTS_NODE.
A zero parent-anchor count adds [WARNING] FLOATING_NODE to Run Notes.
More than one parent anchor adds [WARNING] AMBIGUOUS_ANCHOR to Run Notes.
If checks fail and cannot be auto-repaired conservatively, files remain non-destructively updated.
Failed local checks must be added explicitly to Run Notes.
Uncertain fields after failed checks are set to TBD or UNKNOWN rather than invented.
Dependencies capture information flow, artifact transfer, and explicit constraints stated in sources.
Dependencies do not represent scheduling decisions.
Dependencies do not represent coordination-only relationships.
Dependencies do not represent structural decomposition relationships.
If stage metadata exists in decomposition, it is preferred for interpreting earlier-to-later transfer.
If no stage metadata exists, the project is treated as a single stage.
Same-stage dependencies are permitted only when explicit information or asset transfer is stated.
High-signal extraction includes explicit prerequisites, inputs, and approvals required before work can proceed.
High-signal extraction includes deliverable outputs explicitly consumed by another deliverable.
High-signal extraction includes explicit interfaces requiring specific data or artifacts from another deliverable.
High-signal extraction includes constraints framed as requirements, approvals, artifacts, or required inputs.
High-signal extraction includes traceability statements linking deliverable intent to definition nodes or requirements.
Pure coordination or keep-aligned statements without specific transfer are not extracted.
Structural adjacency obvious from decomposition naming is not extracted as a dependency.
Scheduling dependencies are not extracted unless expressed as input, approval, or artifact constraints.
UPSTREAM means this deliverable requires information or assets from the target.
DOWNSTREAM means this deliverable produces information or assets for the target.
DISCOVER extracts dependency cues from deliverable source documents with evidence.
REGISTER normalizes dependency rows into Dependencies.csv.
VALIDATE performs local quality checks against schema, evidence, and integrity rules.
CONSUME is when downstream workflows read dependencies for planning, reconciliation, or estimating.
REFRESH_OR_RETIRE updates LastSeen on later runs and marks unseen extracted rows RETIRED.
Extraction lifecycle is tracked with FirstSeen, LastSeen, and Status.
Closure lifecycle is tracked with RequiredMaturity, ProposedMaturity, and SatisfactionStatus.
Status tracks whether the dependency relationship is currently observed in source text.
SatisfactionStatus tracks whether the dependency has been fulfilled or remains open.
Dependencies.csv core schema has 29 required columns.
DependencyClass write-form values are ANCHOR and EXECUTION.
AnchorType write-form values are IMPLEMENTS_NODE, TRACES_TO_REQUIREMENT, and NOT_APPLICABLE.
Direction write-form values are UPSTREAM and DOWNSTREAM.
Preferred DependencyType values are PREREQUISITE, INTERFACE, HANDOVER, CONSTRAINT, ENABLES, and OTHER.
Legacy DependencyType values COORDINATION and INFORMATION are read-compatible but not emitted in new extractions.
TargetType write-form values include DELIVERABLE, PACKAGE, WBS_NODE, REQUIREMENT, DOCUMENT, EQUIPMENT, EXTERNAL, and UNKNOWN.
Explicitness write-form values are EXPLICIT and IMPLICIT.
SatisfactionStatus write-form values are TBD, PENDING, IN_PROGRESS, SATISFIED, WAIVED, and NOT_APPLICABLE.
Confidence write-form values are HIGH, MEDIUM, and LOW.
Origin write-form values are DECLARED and EXTRACTED.
Status write-form values are ACTIVE and RETIRED.
Legacy INBOUND and OUTBOUND may appear in older files but are normalized to UPSTREAM and DOWNSTREAM on write.
If RegisterSchemaVersion is missing, it is added and set to v3.1.
EstimateImpactClass and ConsumerHint extension columns may be added when reliably inferred.
EstimateImpactClass and ConsumerHint must not be marked as required columns.
EstimateImpactClass and ConsumerHint are filled conservatively, otherwise omitted or set to TBD.
When CONSUMER_CONTEXT=TASK_ESTIMATING, EXECUTION rows should populate ConsumerHint and EstimateImpactClass when evidence supports them.
ConsumerHint=TASK_ESTIMATING is used when a dependency plausibly affects estimating readiness or scope.
EstimateImpactClass=BLOCKING means a prerequisite, constraint, approval, or input gates meaningful estimating.
EstimateImpactClass=ADVISORY means an interface or handover may change quantities, specifications, or procurement without being a hard gate.
EstimateImpactClass=INFO means informational context has low likelihood of changing totals.
EstimateImpactClass uses TBD when uncertain.
_DEPENDENCIES.md must contain human-owned declared upstream and downstream lists.
_DEPENDENCIES.md must contain the extracted register summary.
_DEPENDENCIES.md must contain run notes and run history.
_DEPENDENCIES.md must contain lifecycle summary.
_DEPENDENCIES.md must contain downstream handoff notes when a consumer context is provided.
Dependencies.csv is the canonical structured dependency register output.
_DEPENDENCIES.md is the human-readable dependency index output.
QA expects source documents in scope not to be modified.
QA expects Dependencies.csv to exist and parse with all 29 required columns.
QA expects every ACTIVE row to include EvidenceFile and SourceRef or location TBD.
QA expects targets not to be invented and UNKNOWN to be permitted.
QA expects non-destructive updates with no row deletions and unseen rows marked RETIRED.
QA expects DependencyID values to be unique within each deliverable register.
QA expects write-form enums to be canonical.
QA expects _DEPENDENCIES.md summary and lifecycle counts to be consistent with Dependencies.csv.
QA expects FLOATING_NODE, AMBIGUOUS_ANCHOR, and MISSING_DECOMPOSITION non-fatal warnings when applicable.
Downstream workflows consume deliverable-local dependency registers.
dependency-extract does not build project-level graphs.
The preferred tool order starts with reasoning-led two-pass extraction over source documents, _REFERENCES.md, and decomposition when available.
The preferred tool order then performs reasoning-led target resolution, row match/merge, and persistence.

Function 5 enum validation uses validate_enum.py.

Reasoning is the primary extraction engine for dependency-extract.
Reasoning governs target resolution, match/merge precedence, enum normalization, index updates, and integrity warnings.
Deterministic tools intervene during Function 5 for schema, enum, and ID-format validation.
